newsitem.title: BRAZIL: RESEARCH ALERT - Salomon says Telebras still a buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Salomon says Telebras still a buy.

text.p: -- Salomon Brothers said it has reiterated its buy rating on Brazilian federal telecommunications giant Telebras

-- The brokerage cited a draft new general telecoms as well as likely tariff rebalancing, upcoming cellular concessions, Telebras' low valuation and good growth prospects for Brazil's telecoms sector.
-- The new law, sent to Congress last week, allows for the break-up and privatization of Telebras as five separate firms, including long-distance company Embratel.
-- But "uncertainties still include how the 27 regional operators will be reconfigured and whether Telebras would remain as a holding company," Salomon said.
-- It also said it believes current minority shareholders will not be hurt by privatization, adding that "minority shareholders (should) become shareholders of operating telecom companies."
-- The government wants lawmakers to approve the new telecom law in 1997's first quarter.
-- However, passage may not happen until the second quarter if a bill allowing President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to stand for re-election in 1998 is not passed, Salomon said.
-- Telebras' ADR ended Monday at 72 1/4 in New York while its preferred closed at 76.25 reais and its voting common ended at 68.90 reais in Sao Paulo.
